response.text:
The Pequod presses west and south into the Indian Ocean, and Ishmael’s tale thickens with the perilous craft of whaling: coiled whale-line that can garrote a man in a blink, iron and wood forged into barbs, and the red business of “cutting-in” a slain sperm whale while sharks and sea-birds riot at the hull. Stubb kills a great fish, smokes his pipe over blue-smoked hemp and hot loggerheads, and banters his way through a midnight feast while the old cook Fleece scolds the sharks; soon the deck is a shambles of hooks, lines, and hymnlike labor as blubber rises like blanket-peels. Ahab’s ship gams with the Jeroboam, whose prophet-mad sailor Gabriel damns any who strike the White Whale; years of rumors harden into a single luminous dread. Ishmael wanders between scalpels and sermons, comparing the heads and bones of right and sperm whales and filing away omens with anatomy, as the crew tows, trims, and sings through long tropic noons.

Ahab’s inward weather darkens, and the shadowy Fedallah becomes his sleepless familiar, prophesying that two hearses will pass upon the sea and that hemp alone can kill him. Perth the blacksmith, ruined ashore, tempers Ahab’s bespoke harpoon in the pagan blood of the crew and the lightning of St. Elmo’s fire, while a typhoon crowns the masts with blue flames and Ahab toasts the unpitying elements. He smashes his quadrant, declares the heavens mute, and trusts only to dead-reckoning and a nail-bright will, even as the compass needles spin and must be remagnetized by hand. On deck, the castaway Pip goes mad after leaping from a whale-boat and, taken to Ahab’s heart, becomes a cracked bell tolling truths the captain half hears; Starbuck, prudent and devout, debates the right to stop a monomaniac soul and stays his hand at the musket. The carpenter turns whalebone and coffin-planks to any purpose, while the ship itself seems bound in some invisible tow-line the captain names Fate.

The Pequod races, trades shouts, and parts from the jubilant Bachelor heavy with oil, then passes the Delight sewing a dead whaleman into canvas and the grieving Rachel whose captain begs help to find his lost boy; Ahab hardens his heart and sails on. Queequeg sickens, orders his canoe-coffin made and carves it with his own tattooed cosmology, only to recover, whereupon the box is later rigged as a life-buoy. Storms, sermons, and smithy sparks braid into a single cable of foreboding, and Ahab’s eyes are fixed so long at the masthead that his soul seems nailed there with the Spanish doubloon he promised to the man who first raises Moby Dick.

At last the cry comes: there she blows, a hump like a snow-hill. Over three relentless days the White Whale breaches and batters, stove-boats whirl in snarled lines, and Fedallah vanishes only to reappear lashed dead to the leviathan’s back, fulfilling the first hearse. On the second day the whale rams the Pequod and swims off in a traveling wake of foam, while Starbuck pleads for home and Ahab refuses, hoisting himself aloft on a new ivory leg and old vows. On the third day Ahab drives in his iron “for hate’s sake,” the running line whips, and hemp bows him like a string—then strangles him clean off the thwart as Moby Dick wheels and smashes the ship. The Pequod founders amid a ring of spinning wreckage; Tashtego, nailing the flag to the sinking mast, snags a sky-hawk and goes down wreathed in canvas and feathers, the second hearse of American wood fulfilled.

All collapses, and then the sea rolls on as it rolled five thousand years ago. Held up by Queequeg’s coffin, now a life-buoy, Ishmael alone survives the vortex of lines, iron, faith, and fury; he floats through a long dirge of foam and sky until the devious-cruising Rachel, still searching for her children, finds and rescues another orphan. Moby-Dick’s last pages draw tight the book’s braided themes: a working world of ropes, iron, sail, and human song set against the inscrutable sea; a crew pressed into one man’s monomania until prophecy, pride, and Fate close their jaws. Man’s instruments and ideas—quadrants, compasses, sermons, and songs—glitter for a moment and fail, while the whale’s blind forehead and the ocean’s old indifference endure. In the end, the tale is both a craftsman’s ledger and a philosopher’s lament, and the only witness left to tell it counts his heartbeats on a borrowed coffin in the wide, unanswering blue.
